dbRoles.anon: Anonymous public endpoints (application-*, public-module-*) reach the DB only through service_role inside the function, so anon needs no table privilege for them.
dbRoles.authenticated: CRITICAL: both WORKS employees AND logged-in GUESTs run as this single Postgres role. The guest custom JWT carries role:"authenticated" (guestAccount.ts:328) and is signed with GUEST_JWT_SECRET, which crypto.ts:15 states must equal the project JWT secret. Therefore every GRANT ... TO authenticated is reachable by a guest session and is separated from employee data by RLS predicates alone.

findings.severity: P0 (latent — no send path exists today)
findings.title: notifications-dispatch accepts an arbitrary recipient and an arbitrary credential-bearing template from any Supabase Auth user
findings.evidence: supabase/functions/notifications-dispatch/index.ts:14-24. Auth is `supabaseAdmin().auth.getUser(token)` and nothing else. `to`, `templateCode` and `variables` come from the request body and are forwarded verbatim to sendNotification.
findings.why: The template registry (_shared/notifications.ts:15-62) contains GUEST_OTP, GUEST_PASSWORD_RESET (with a caller-supplied {{link}}), and GUEST_INVITE_NEW (which instructs the reader to log in with their registered phone digits). Any holder of any employee session could therefore send an arbitrary address a message that renders as an official Y&Archer password-reset carrying an attacker-chosen URL, from the company's own verified sender.
findings.currentlyBlockedBy: _shared/notifications.ts:108-118 — no provider adapter exists, so every keyed send returns ok:false and nothing leaves. On a local http stack with no key the body is console-logged. The exposure arms itself the moment an adapter lands.
findings.compoundedBy: _shared/cors.ts:22-24 grace mode (any origin when ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset) and the absence of requireStrictBrowserOrigin on this function.
findings.notAffected: Guests cannot reach it: a guest custom JWT has no auth.users row, so getUser fails. service_role key is not a user token either. The gap is employee-side, not guest-side.

findings.title: notifications-dispatch has zero callers anywhere and writes no audit record
findings.evidence: No reference in apps/** or packages/** (0 hits). No pg_net/net.http_post call from any migration. In-app notification is already handled DB-side by triggers inserting public.notifications (20260722120000:89, 20260731110000:75,119, 20260905200000:193). public.notification_logs exists (20260705230000) but notifications-dispatch never writes to it.
findings.why: A generic send primitive that nothing uses is pure attack surface, and it would leave no trace if used. Note the caller IS authenticated — employee Supabase Auth accounts exist and pass auth.getUser. The defect was the absence of AUTHORIZATION (role, send authority, recipient ownership), not the absence of authentication.

findings.title: apps/guest calls an edge function that does not exist in the repo
findings.evidence: apps/guest/src/pages/TempGuestPage.tsx:28 POSTs to `${functionsBase}/guest-temp-resolve`. No supabase/functions/guest-temp-resolve directory exists.
findings.why: Either a deployed function exists with no source under version control — in which case its authorization is unreviewable and unreproducible from a clean replay — or the temporary-guest page is silently broken. Both need an answer before AUTHZ closes. This is a source-side observation; the deployed function list is not visible from here.

findings.title: Four functions resolve the caller without the is_active / external-role checks that internalAuth performs
findings.evidence: _shared/aiFill/run.ts:99-106, _shared/aiFill/extractRun.ts:150-157, material-download/index.ts:43-49, employee-create/index.ts:66-72 all do `select id from users where auth_user_id = ... and deleted_at is null` with no `is_active` filter. link-metadata/index.ts:63 does not even look at public.users. Contrast _shared/internalAuth.ts:22, which checks is_active AND excludes the three external user_types.
findings.why: A deactivated employee whose Supabase Auth session is still alive passes these gates. Impact is bounded — the aiFill functions immediately re-ask canWrite/canCreate under the caller token, material-download re-queries rows under the caller token, and employee-create still requires super_admin or management write — so this is a defence-in-depth inconsistency, not an open door. But it means "deactivate the employee" is not by itself a complete revocation for these five paths; the RLS helper behind current_app_user_id() is what actually has to hold the line.
findings.recommendation: Route all five through resolveInternalCaller(). Out of scope for AUTHZ-1/2; log as a bounded follow-up.

findings.kind: deployment configuration gate — NOT an authorization finding
findings.title: CORS grace mode leaves 18 of 22 functions callable from any origin
findings.evidence: _shared/cors.ts:22-24 returns true for every origin with only a console.warn when ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset. requireStrictBrowserOrigin (cors.ts:72) refuses that grace, but only ai-minute-draft, stt-transcribe, meeting-recording-playback and meeting-recording-process call it.
findings.why: guest-auth-login, guest-auth-password, employee-create and material-download are all reachable cross-origin until the operations secret is set. The code already documents this as a pre-production requirement; it belongs on the deploy checklist, not in a code change.
findings.clarification: CORS is not a server-side authorization control and no data is exposed by this item alone. Every function still enforces its own token check and RLS. The only effect is that the browser-reachable call surface is not narrowed until ALLOWED_ORIGINS is set. Do not treat this as an access-control gap.

findings.severity: P0 for the ACL decision (not an exposure)
findings.kind: role-collision the grant matrix must account for
findings.title: GUEST sessions and WORKS employees share the single `authenticated` Postgres role
findings.evidence: _shared/guestAccount.ts:325-341 signs `role: "authenticated"`; _shared/crypto.ts:15 records that the signing secret must equal the project JWT secret so PostgREST trusts it; apps/guest/src/lib/supabase.ts:10-14 sends that token as the Authorization header against the anon key client.
findings.why: Every `grant ... to authenticated` the ACL worker writes is simultaneously a grant to logged-in external startups and experts. Nothing at the privilege layer separates them — only the RLS predicate does. Concretely, apps/guest reads program_announcements, program_modules, program_posts, program_links, program_notices, program_overviews, attachments and reads+inserts program_questions with that role. The finite grant set must be justified against the guest threat model, not only the employee one.

findings.severity: DECISION INPUT (corrected 2026-09-12 — my earlier reading was wrong)
findings.kind: live DELETE requiring an explicit grant decision
findings.title: capital_call_payments DELETE is a LIVE client path, not dead code
findings.evidence: apps/works/src/features/fund/hooks.ts:322-343 useDeleteCapitalCall — deletes capital_call_payments rows by capital_call_id, then soft-deletes the capital_calls row. Wired at apps/works/src/features/fund/CapitalCallPanel.tsx:28 behind a confirm dialog.
findings.why: authenticated therefore genuinely needs DELETE on capital_call_payments, or this feature breaks. 20260912025406:21-23 deliberately grants no DELETE anywhere, citing 3_database_rls_policy_matrix.md §2.5. This is the one documented exception the grant matrix has to decide explicitly rather than by omission — including whether a `for delete` policy exists to back it.
findings.correction: My first pass claimed set_capital_call_payments (fund/hooks.ts:427) superseded this path. It does NOT. That RPC is the atomic replace-set used when editing one call's payment lines; useDeleteCapitalCall is the separate delete-the-whole-call path. The source comment at hooks.ts:315-320 states the reason for the hard DELETE: hiding only the call would leave its payment rows counted in fund_lps.paid_amount and funds aggregates, contradicting the confirm dialog text.
findings.owner: Passed to the ACL worker by the parent.

findings.title: partner-docs bucket retains its row after its policies were dropped
findings.evidence: Bucket created 20260903210000:209; all three storage.objects policies dropped by 20260911054939:21-23. No browser or edge client references it.

nonFindings: The three anonymous endpoints (public-module-get, public-module-file, application-form-get, application-submit) use service_role deliberately and are gated by a single unit-tested pure function (publicModuleLinkGate.ts, publicModuleLinkGate.test.ts). Bypassing RLS here is the design, not a defect — the gate is the authorization and each function narrows its own output.

guest-access-invite and guest-password-reset do NOT use service_role for the authorization decision; they delegate to SECURITY INVOKER RPCs under the caller token and only then escalate. This is the correct pattern and should not be flagged.

A SECURITY DEFINER function with public EXECUTE is not automatically a defect. The aiFill profiles depend on can_write_startup / can_create_startup / can_write_ma_seller / can_create_ma_seller / attachment_refs being callable by authenticated — that is the mechanism by which the edge function refuses to copy the permission predicate. Revoking EXECUTE on these would break the AI-fill authorization path, not harden it.
entity_contributions INSERT by authenticated is intentional and documented (docs_master/CLAUDE.md §3): the actor column is overwritten by a BEFORE INSERT trigger.

unknowns.note: Everything in tables[].grantInSource is migration TEXT, not catalog state. Legacy auto-exposed privileges from before auto_expose_new_tables was unset are invisible from source and are exactly what the ACL worker's replayed catalog must enumerate.

unknowns.dynamicDdl: Policies for at least these migrations are created inside `execute format(...)` loops and cannot be read by grep: 20260705150500_ac_rls, 20260705170000_fund_schema, 20260705180000_mna_schema, 20260705200000_project_schema, 20260705210000_management_schema, 20260803230100_program_module_content, 20260903100000_program_module_ledger_unify, 20260903110000_module_content_rls_polymorphic, 20260903120000_guest_portal_all_program_workspaces. A naive scan reports funds, investments, capital_calls, assets, kpi_records, dept_budgets, application_forms and application_submissions as having no policy; they do, via those loops. No policy conclusion should be drawn from this artifact.
unknowns.note: NO RLS BEHAVIOUR IS VERIFIED BY THIS ARTIFACT. Nothing here establishes that any policy exists, that its predicate is correct, or that it actually restricts rows. Policy text was grepped only to spot obvious mismatches, and that grep is known to be wrong for every table whose policies are built in `execute format(...)` loops. Row-level behaviour must come from the replayed catalog plus supabase/tests.

The 80 RPCs are listed as demand only. secdef / search_path / EXECUTE grants unverified from source.
guest-temp-resolve (E-3) cannot be resolved from the repo. Requires whoever can see the deployment.

supabase/config.toml has no [functions] section and no verify_jwt setting anywhere in the repo. Whether the platform pre-validates Authorization before the handler runs — and therefore whether the guest custom JWT and the anonymous endpoints behave as the code assumes — is a deployment fact this audit cannot establish.
Both carry grants in migration source but have zero browser callsites in this scan. Either RPC-only or dead. Candidates for revocation review.

edgeFunctions.name: guest-auth-login
edgeFunctions.authMechanism: NONE (anonymous). Credentials in body: {email,password}. Anon apikey header only.
edgeFunctions.callerGate: handler.ts:69 findAccountByEmail restricts to user_type in (external_startup,external_expert,temporary_guest), is_active, deleted_at null. handler.ts:73 account lockout 5/15min. handler.ts:79-89 initial password = ledger phone digits ONLY when guest_credentials.password_hash is null.
edgeFunctions.serviceRole: YES — supabaseAdmin() for the whole flow (index.ts:6,9).
edgeFunctions.validationBeforePrivilege: Uniform 401 for unknown account and bad password (enumeration guard). No session issued in initial-password state — only a 10-min change ticket (aud=guest-password-change).
edgeFunctions.verdict: INTENTIONAL protected server path. Matches user-fixed GUEST policy (3_9_1 §6): email ID + initial registered phone before personal password, no session before password set.

edgeFunctions.name: guest-auth-password
edgeFunctions.authMechanism: Two modes. SET: {changeTicket,newPassword} — HS256 ticket, aud=guest-password-change, 10 min. CHANGE: {currentPassword,newPassword} + Bearer guest session JWT.
edgeFunctions.callerGate: handler.ts:107 verifyJwt aud check; :117 refuses SET when a hash already exists unless ticket carries rst=true (reset path); handler.ts:136 verifyGuestSession (session_version re-checked against DB); :145 current password re-verified; :120/:151 passwordPolicyError forbids reusing the ledger phone.
edgeFunctions.serviceRole: YES — supabaseAdmin().
edgeFunctions.validationBeforePrivilege: Policy check precedes savePassword; savePassword clears reset token, attempts, lock.
edgeFunctions.verdict: INTENTIONAL protected server path.

edgeFunctions.name: guest-auth-refresh
edgeFunctions.authMechanism: Bearer guest custom JWT (HS256, GUEST_JWT_SECRET, aud=authenticated).
edgeFunctions.callerGate: _shared/guestSession.ts:41 verifyGuestSession — signature + exp + aud + DB re-read of users(is_active, deleted_at, session_version). index.ts:51 loadOpenParticipations re-applies the RLS predicate (login_status in INVITED/ACTIVE + ledger guest_access_ends_at). :75 dead/deleted program => 401.
edgeFunctions.serviceRole: YES — supabaseAdmin(); response fields are hand-narrowed (index.ts:83-107) and INTERNAL_ONLY_STATUSES (PROPOSED/SELECTED/NOT_SELECTED) are nulled out.
edgeFunctions.validationBeforePrivilege: Session -> open participation -> live program, all before any data is returned.
edgeFunctions.verdict: INTENTIONAL protected server path. Deliberately avoids granting guests SELECT on programs.

edgeFunctions.name: guest-auth-context
edgeFunctions.authMechanism: Either {selectTicket} (aud=guest-context-select, 10 min) or Bearer guest session JWT.
edgeFunctions.callerGate: index.ts:38-52 resolveUserId; :78 requested participantId must appear in loadParticipations() for THAT account, else 403. Explicit anti-IDOR comment at index.ts:14-16.
edgeFunctions.serviceRole: YES — supabaseAdmin().
edgeFunctions.validationBeforePrivilege: Server re-derives the allowed participation set; the client-supplied id is only used as a lookup key.
edgeFunctions.verdict: INTENTIONAL protected server path.

edgeFunctions.name: guest-password-reset
edgeFunctions.authMechanism: SEND: Bearer internal caller JWT + {userId}. CONSUME: {resetToken}, anonymous.
edgeFunctions.callerGate: SEND — index.ts:52 caller.rpc(authorize_guest_password_reset) executed with the CALLER token via anon key client, so SECURITY INVOKER + RLS decide; 42501 -> 403. CONSUME — index.ts:108 token looked up by sha256 hash, expiry enforced, single use (:124 nulls the hash).
edgeFunctions.serviceRole: YES, but only AFTER the RPC authorization returns (index.ts:62). Comment at :13-16 states the reason.
edgeFunctions.validationBeforePrivilege: Recipient is read from the account ledger (index.ts:83), never from the request body. Caller receives {ok,notified} only — no token, no contact.
edgeFunctions.verdict: INTENTIONAL protected server path. This is the reference pattern SEC-1 should copy.

edgeFunctions.name: guest-access-invite
edgeFunctions.callerGate: index.ts:53 caller.rpc(open_program_guest_access) under the caller token (anon key client) — RLS/invoker decides; 42501 -> 403. No service_role anywhere in this function.
edgeFunctions.serviceRole: NO.
edgeFunctions.validationBeforePrivilege: Recipients come back FROM the RPC (email/phone read from the ledger server-side), not from the request. Send failures do not roll back the access opening (documented at :104).
edgeFunctions.verdict: INTENTIONAL protected server path. Best-in-repo example.

edgeFunctions.name: employee-create
edgeFunctions.callerGate: index.ts:63 db.auth.getUser(token); :66 public.users row (deleted_at null); :74 super_admin OR :76-83 workspace_permissions(management)=write with expires_at honoured; else 403.

edgeFunctions.verdict: INTENTIONAL protected server path. Note: caller row lookup omits is_active (see finding E-4).

edgeFunctions.name: material-download
edgeFunctions.authMechanism: Dual: Supabase Auth JWT (internal) OR guest custom JWT. index.ts:37-70 resolveCaller.

edgeFunctions.serviceRole: YES — only for access_logs insert (:112) and createSignedUrl (:121). Never for the authorization query.
edgeFunctions.validationBeforePrivilege: access_logs insert failure blocks the signed URL (:112-120) — "no log, no export". TTL 60 s. LINK-kind attachments short-circuit (:107).
edgeFunctions.verdict: INTENTIONAL protected server path. Sole download path since 20260716130300 revoked storage.objects SELECT.
